findings.reason: The protected source is a clear conventional two-dimensional Fenwick tree. It copies current values for assignment deltas, uses exact row and column ancestor walks, computes rectangles by four-prefix inclusion-exclusion, and keeps the batch adapter small and order-preserving. Its compound row_index and column_index names describe genuine data-structure coordinates, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 308 and its Python NumMatrix surface. The Reference accurately separates native update and sumRegion operations from the app batch contract, and preserves the single source trace with explanation, all ten constraints, inclusive rectangle semantics, and an accessible rendering of the source illustration.

The immutable native NumMatrix remains tied to verified submission 2064366450. It and the protected app-local class have identical value storage, two-dimensional Fenwick construction and updates, prefix traversal, and inclusion-exclusion; solve is the permitted app-only operation adapter.

The legal 8x8, 24x24, and 48x48 tiers span 36x in cell count and run 2mn alternating wide queries and assignments while remaining below the 5,000-call cap. The current source passes the performance path at +0.01 relative growth and 1.00x; a correct direct rectangle scan fails only scaling at +0.18.

The previously recorded legacy conflict has now been inspected and repaired: after assigning the center to -5 and the top-right cell to 0, rectangle (0,1)..(1,2) sums to 3, not 1. A direct mutable-matrix oracle verifies the corrected suite and the protected implementation.

The Approach now defines m, n, and q before the manifest bound. Its rectangle ownership, delta propagation, prefix tiling, inclusion-exclusion proof, straightforward build cost, per-operation cost, and boundary notes match the protected source exactly.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against authenticated source evidence, including the class operations, source trace and explanation, all ten constraints, and the informational equivalent of the before-and-after source image.

coverage: The sole authenticated source trace appears first with the exact matrix, query, update, repeated query, and app-adapted outputs 8 and 10.
Two invented rows are now trials rather than source samples, and the formerly hidden interleaved row is visible with its false final expectation corrected from 1 to 3.
A one-cell matrix covers both minimum dimensions; one-row and one-column matrices exercise the maximum width and height of 200 and their endpoint indices.
Initial values and assignments touch -1,000 and 1,000, with negative totals, sign-changing deltas, repeated assignments, and a zero-delta update.

Full-matrix, interior, row, column, single-cell, and opposite-corner rectangles verify inclusive bounds and all four-prefix inclusion-exclusion terms; an update-only sequence verifies the app adapter's empty result contract.

A direct mutable-matrix oracle verified all 13 authored results and all three benchmark results; the protected source also matched it on 53,184 exhaustive legal operation sequences over every matrix shape up to 2 by 2 with values and assignments from {-1, 0, 1}.
All 13 correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 8 by 8, 24 by 24, and 48 by 48 alternating workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
